close_reason: Landed. upload_blob now takes UploadBlobParams<'_>; the four positional args (upload_url_template, account_id, data, content_type) are gone. Three existing test sites migrated to the typed shape (two error-path in tests/client_tests.rs, one streaming-cap in tests/streaming_cap_tests.rs). New positive round-trip test test_upload_blob_typed_params_round_trip in tests/client_tests.rs asserts the wire request — URL template expansion, Content-Type header, body bytes — and the parsed BlobUploadResponse shape. Re-exported at the crate root alongside DownloadBlobParams.
description: crate-jmap-base-client/src/blob.rs:219-225 declares pub async fn upload_blob(&self, upload_url_template: &str, account_id: &str, data: bytes::Bytes, content_type: &str) -> ... — four positional parameters including three string-typed ones (the template URL, the account_id, the content_type). The download_blob counterpart in the same file (blob.rs:324-336) was already refactored to take DownloadBlobParams<'a> precisely because six positional &str args invited call-site confusion. upload_blob still has the older shape and is one fat-finger away from upload_blob(content_type, account_id, data, template_url) compiling silently and POSTing the wrong URL with the wrong header. Recommendation: introduce UploadBlobParams<'a> mirroring DownloadBlobParams<'a>: { upload_url_template, account_id, content_type, data }. Caller writes a named-field struct literal at every call site, gains documentation, and adding an optional field (per-call timeout override, body integrity hint, etc.) becomes a non-breaking minor-version bump. The current shape locks the positional order in for SemVer.
title: upload_blob takes four positional &str args — same parameter-confusion DownloadBlobParams already solved
